newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany awards two new public phone licences.
newsitem.headline: Germany awards two new public phone licences.

text.p: The German government on Thursday said it has awarded two new public telephone operating licences to Mannesmann Arcor AG and Teleglobe GmbH as part its efforts to open telecommunications to competition next year.
The two companies will be allowed to provide basic telephone services to the public nation-wide from January, when the monopoly of Deutsche Telekom AG is abolished.

The post and telecommunications ministry is currently handling applications for Class 4 and Class 3 licences, which regulate the operation of basic public phone services and telecommunications transmission services respectively.
Arcor is the telecommunications joint venture of Mannesmann AG, the German railway, AT&T, the European Unisource venture and Deutsche Bank.
The ministry added in a statement that it awarded two further Class 3 licences to the German subsidiary of Britain's Colt Plc on Wednesday. It had not announced this previously.

The ministry has awarded a total of 22 telecommunications operators licences so far -- five for basic phone services and 17 for telecommunications transmission. It said five companies now have licences for both categories.
